question.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2-5\text{i} \\ \text{i}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3+\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}]\ne C,
$$

while

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) \\ -\text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overset{―}{\lambda }=-3-\text{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda .$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overset{―}{v},$ the complex conjugate of $v.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}-2+5\text{i} \\ -\text{i}\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
